Marissa / Dev — dropping a champ enablement pack you can use directly. Putting this here so Sophie can forward to Rajiv (I've also kept language that works for an exec email).

Executive one-paragraph (for Rajiv):
Redwood Inference delivers predictable, low-latency LLM inference that reduces per-request cost and developer maintenance overhead. For teams like Finovate Bank, typical outcomes are 30-50% reduction in per-call unit cost through batching + KV caching, 3-4x faster time-to-market for new LLM features using the Redwood API, and predictable capacity via Dedicated slots that remove surprise spend during spikes.

ROI bullets (short):
- Unit-cost reduction: 30-50% typical after batching & caching (example: payments notifier reduced token cost by 38%).
- Developer productivity: cut from 6w to 2w for model integration (standardized SDKs + docs).
- Latency/SLO: 95th percentile tail latency under 250ms for targeted workloads (with Dedicated).
- Operational risk mitigation: built-in model fallbacks + region routing to avoid outages during vendor incidents.

Security & procurement quick answers (for Priya / Rajesh):
- SOC2 Type II report available; we can share the auditor attestation (see attached security overview).
- KMS integrations: support for customer-managed keys (AWS KMS, GCP KMS); HSM options available for Private deployments.
- Data residency: hosting in customer's VPC or region-specific Dedicated; documented data flows and audit logs for compliance.
- Procurement: standard SOW + Master Services Agreement; we accept PO and have expedited vendor onboarding for enterprise deals.

Suggested short email Sophie can forward to Rajiv:
"Rajiv — quick note on why Redwood would be a solid fit for Finovate Bank: predictable latency and a clear path to cut inference unit cost by ~30-50% while reducing integration time. Happy to run a short POC and surface concrete savings for one of your high-volume flows. —Rishi"

Pricing anchor guidance for initial commercial conversation: lead with value (unit economics) not absolute rate. For example, propose a committed Dedicated baseline that aligns with peak traffic; use burst capacity for spiky flows and show modeled cost per 100k requests.

Attached: SLA_price_deck.pdf (public price + SLA examples). Use the exec paragraph + ROI bullets in the one-pager and the short email for Sophie.

Cheers,
Rishi
VP, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
